sentences.text: Researchers applied a deep learning algorithm to isolate lower back muscles from patient-specific CT scans.
They then constructed two computer simulations, one including the rib cage and relaxed muscles and a control with only the spine, to test movement during twisting, side bending, and forward bending.
The rib cage and relaxed muscles limited twisting the most, causing the upper back to become stiffer while the lower back and waist area moved more than in the spine-only model.
For side and forward bending, these structures reduced movement across all parts of the spine.
The authors suggest that front-to-back spinal balance depends mostly on active muscle contraction, possibly because the rib cage anchors the upper spine and forces the lower spine to compensate.
